page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.4xlarge is a general purpose server instance powered by AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features 16 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache, along with hardware-assisted cryptographic AES instruction support. The server contains 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It provides a 33 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No local storage is bundled, requiring the use of remote network storage volumes, and it includes no discrete hardware GPUs.

Benchmark analysis demonstrates high memory throughput and multi-threaded processing capacity. The server achieves top-tier results in PassMark memory testing (score of 3379.27) and strong uncached memory bandwidth, delivering 296.88 GB/sec in read operations and 138.33 GB/sec in write operations. Multi-core performance is robust, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 15946.0, strong bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 203.02 GB/sec, and strong PassMark database operations at 24236.19. In contrast, single-core metrics fall into middle-tier bands, such as a Geekbench single-core score of 1891.0. In addition, CPU-driven language model inference is weak, registering 48.9 tokens per second for small-model generation and 31.28 tokens per second for medium-model prompt processing.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the instance stems from its dedicated ARM core density and high memory bandwidth without the premium associated with GPU hardware or specialized high-RAM tiers. However, operational tradeoffs include the absence of local NVMe storage and lack of x86 vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX. The instance profile fits multi-threaded server-side tasks including relational databases, caching layers, containerized backend services, code compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gb.4xlarge is an ARM-based general purpose instance built on the Nitro System and powered by a 16-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. It delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs with single threading, 64.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and a 33 Gbps baseline network capacity. The platform does not bundle local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. Benchmark results show standout memory performance, marked by uncached read throughput of 296.88 GB/sec and strong multi-core database processing. Single-core performance and CPU-based LLM generation remain average to weak. By providing dedicated physical cores paired with high-bandwidth memory, the m8gb.4xlarge serves as a cost-efficient host for enterprise web serving, relational databases, CI/CD pipelines, and general containerized application tiers.
